result.text: Title: Instruct an artist to create a 3D model print it on a 3D printer When craving a custom 3D model, as a first step you have to instruct an artist to create a project for you.
First you have to send him several sketches, and then tell him what to change until you are satisfied with the result.
After that, you choose a plastic color you want to use for 3D printing.
If you have the color at home (in stock), you check how much color you have left.
If it's under 100 grams, you put it on your shopping list.
If you do not have the color at home, you order it.
When you have the plastic, you can turn the printer on and heat up the bed and the extruder (it continuously sends you back its status).
While doing that, you can generate the gcode file for your printer out of the STL sent to you by the artist.
After that you print the model.

result.process_description:
Title: Instruct an artist to create a 3D model print it on a 3D printer

When craving a custom 3D model, as a first step you have to instruct an artist to create a project for you.
First you have to send him several sketches, and then tell him what to change until you are satisfied with the result.
After that, you choose a plastic color you want to use for 3D printing.
If you have the color at home (in stock), you check how much color you have left.
If it's under 100 grams, you put it on your shopping list.
If you do not have the color at home, you order it.
When you have the plastic, you can turn the printer on and heat up the bed and the extruder (it continuously sends you back its status).
While doing that, you can generate the gcode file for your printer out of the STL sent to you by the artist.
After that you print the model.

result.rule: Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.

result.rule: When the description says to send a request or provide input to another participant and then make later work depend on receiving that participant’s response: Model the response as a receiving activity or message-catching event, as appropriate, and connect the sending activity to it with a sequence flow before the dependent work.

When the description says to send work to another participant and request changes until an acceptance condition is met, without describing distinct incoming messages for each iteration: Model one response-receiving activity or message-catching event before the acceptance decision, and loop the exchange through that decision; do not add separate receiving elements for inferred intermediate responses.

When the description states that a participant submits information and that it is subsequently entered into a record or system.: Model submission and recording as distinct activities connected in the stated order.

When the description says work may be evaluated and changed repeatedly in response to evaluation feedback: Model a decision-controlled cycle that routes work needing further changes back for another evaluation and lets work needing no further changes proceed. Model providing feedback as a separate activity when the description states that it is performed work.

Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
